propositions: The retired LLM retrigger word 'recheck-review' collides with an external CI ChatOps substring matcher (lfit/releng-gerrit_to_platform) that maps 'recheck' to 'verify', causing spurious CI run cancellations when the word is posted as a comment.
The bot's own reply texts (_ACCEPTED_MESSAGE and _refusal_message) embed the retired trigger word, causing the bot's own Gerrit comments to re-dispatch the Verified workflow.

A new trigger token 'rerun-llm-review' was chosen because it contains no substring collision with any [mapping "comment-added"] key in the ini template and is validated by tests that parse the ini at runtime.

The retired word triggers a best-effort refusal reply (posted only after project and change-key guards) that descriptively names the new trigger without spelling the old word, preventing self-dispatch from the refusal.

All contributor-facing documentation was updated to reference only the new trigger word, with the old word surviving only in retrigger.py and its test suite, and the ini template was left unchanged on the CI side.
